clue.text: Tavern healthy Cockney used, hard by river

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of a word, so the word for healthy loses its opening letter

parts.note: hale means healthy and robust
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A Cockney who is in fine fettle uses a pub that sits close to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney used' signals the dropped H of London speech, giving 'ALE; the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a pub, a synonym for tavern.

clue.text: Psalm-book's title concealed by opponent and friend

parts.note: anti is a person who is against something, an opponent

indicators.note: the title is hidden away inside the word for friend, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: pal is an informal word for a friend
Hon, short for Honourable, is a title

explanation.surface: The heading of a hymnal is kept out of sight by an enemy and a mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed by' puts the title inside the friend; Hon (Honourable) is a courtesy title in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiphonal is a book of chants and psalms sung responsively by two choirs, so it counts as a psalm-book.

clue.text: River that's unknown, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: x is the standard algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone is informed that a waterway has no name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England, so it is an example of a river.

clue.text: Travelling in 'coach visible to audience

parts.note: if you are travelling in a vehicle you are on it
a stage is short for a stagecoach, the apostrophe marking the clipped word

explanation.surface: Riding in a coach where the onlookers can see you.
explanation.walkthrough: A stagecoach was a horse-drawn coach running between stages on a route.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor on the stage is in view of the people watching, so the phrase is a synonym for visible to the audience.

clue.text: Violin-maker's note about jazz with diverse sound

indicators.note: the note's two letters go around the jazz word, one piece wrapping the other

parts.note: si is an older name for the seventh note of the scale, now usually te
trad is short for traditional jazz

indicators.note: sound tells us to take what is heard, a word pronounced like the synonym for diverse

parts.note: various means diverse or assorted

explanation.surface: A craftsman's musical tone concerns jazz with a varied noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the note around the jazz; 'sound' signals a near-homophone, the Latinised spelling of the maker's name drops the O of the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Stradivari, Latinised as Stradivarius, was the famous Italian maker of violins in Cremona.

clue.text: Story doesn't begin to identify farming land!

indicators.note: the word for story is to lose its opening letter, as if it failed to start

parts.note: a parable is a story told to teach a moral

explanation.surface: A tale that never gets going is used to point out some cropland.
explanation.walkthrough: PARABLE without its first letter P gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable is used as a noun for land that is ploughed and used for growing crops, i.e. farming land.

clue.text: Start to rent an instrument mostly for making pasta

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here from rent

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, here A

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the instrument is dropped

parts.note: a violin is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone begins hiring a musical instrument for some purpose of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: R, then A, then VIOLI (VIOLIN without its N).
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pockets of pasta stuffed with meat or cheese, an example of pasta.

clue.text: Where Americans drink or hear blues, perhaps?

definitions.text: Where Americans drink or hear blues, perhaps?

parts.words: Where Americans drink or hear blues, perhaps?
parts.note: in the US the word names both a cheap saloon serving drinks from casks and a rough piano blues style born in such places

explanation.definitionFit: In American usage it is a cheap bar and also a style of honky-tonk blues piano played there.

clue.text: A woman's right, always!

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman insists she is always right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, a synonym for always.

clue.text: Gold on this island? Silver, too

definitions.text: Gold on this island? Silver, too

parts.words: Gold on this island? Silver, too
parts.note: the clue alludes to the Stevenson adventure novel about an island of buried gold, whose pirate is Long John Silver

explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the pirate in Stevenson's novel, so silver is a pun as well as precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold and silver are both precious riches, i.e. buried hoard, and the island of the novel holds them.

clue.text: Disinclined to write a few lines

parts.note: a verse is a short group of lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to put down a short poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means having a strong dislike or reluctance, a synonym for disinclined.

clue.text: Sucker taken in by fraud is skilled marksman

indicators.note: the sucker is held inside the word for fraud, one piece enclosed by the other

parts.note: a sharper is a swindler or cheat
a sucker in gardening is a shoot springing from a plant's root or stem

explanation.surface: A gullible victim is fooled by a con artist who is in fact a crack shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe, but it is the botanical sense: SHOOT goes into SHARP...ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpshooter is an expert shot, a synonym for a skilled marksman.

clue.text: Be fussy selecting cream with sweets, say

parts.note: the pick of something is its best part, its cream
and means with, joined to

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the word aloud and take a word sounding the same

parts.note: chews are chewy sweets

explanation.surface: Someone is picky when choosing whipped cream alongside confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick and choose is the idiom for being overly selective, fussy when making a selection.

clue.text: Old PM is corporation treasurer

definitions.meaning: Neville ... was British Prime Minister 1937 to 1940
the officer who looks after the finances of a city corporation, such as the City of London

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a former prime minister, and also the title of the official who manages a city corporation's funds.

clue.text: Crime that somehow involves one in manipulation of figures

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the one goes inside the rearranged letters
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A felony that in some way involves someone in fiddling the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the two words into ARITHMETC; 'involves' slips the one in before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic is the branch of mathematics dealing with calculation with numbers, i.e. working with figures.

clue.text: Stain finally removed from flowery spout

indicators.note: removed from tells us that letter is taken out of the following word

parts.note: ornate means flowery, highly decorated in style

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word stain

explanation.surface: A mark has at last been cleaned off a decorative water spout.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the last letter of Stain, comes out of ORNATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout and to orate both mean to hold forth pompously, so they are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Skilled worker. — one disappearing across river

indicators.note: the disappearing one lies across, i.e. spans, the river letter, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a vanisher is one who vanishes

explanation.surface: A craftsman described as someone who disappears over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A varnisher is a tradesman who applies varnish to furniture or woodwork, a type of skilled worker.

clue.text: Sound country girl's first perfume ingredient

indicators.note: sound tells us to take something heard, a phrase pronounced like the answer

parts.note: with the girl first: the name Amber, then the country Greece

explanation.surface: A healthy rural girl's very first scent component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound country girl' reads as a healthy rural lass; instead Amber (girl) comes first, then Greece (country), said together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales long used as a fixative in perfumes, an example of an ingredient.

clue.text: Called about related position on graded scale

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for called surrounds the word for related

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called
kin means related by family

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned concerning a family member's place in a league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the word for called around the family word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a place in a hierarchy or league, i.e. a position on a graded scale.

clue.text: Climb Everest, for example

definitions.meaning: to climb something is to go up it
Everest is a mountain, called a ... in names such as ... Everest

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to go up, a synonym for climb; as a noun it is a mountain, of which Everest is an example.

clue.text: Fail to meet one acting for embassy

parts.note: to miss someone is to fail to meet them
I is the Roman numeral for one
an actor who is on is performing on stage

explanation.surface: Someone fails to meet a person who represents the embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is a body of diplomats posted abroad, a synonym for an embassy.

clue.text: Lose energy, being loco?

definitions.meaning: loco is short for locomotive, and a steam engine literally stops when its steam is gone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loco' looks like Spanish for crazy, but here it is a railway locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to tire and lose momentum, from steam engines grinding to a halt.

clue.text: Drive to present information favourably

definitions.meaning: a short drive in a car
to put a favourable slant on news, as press officers do

explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short trip in a car, and to spin is to slant news in a favourable light.

clue.text: Calm clan leader wearing tartan cloth

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the cloth goes around the letter

parts.note: plaid is a tartan woollen cloth worn in the Scottish Highlands

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here from clan

explanation.surface: A serene Highland chief dressed in a tartan.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the first letter of clan, goes inside PLAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means peaceful and not easily upset, a synonym for calm.

clue.text: Books on jazz style making harsh noise

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the books follow the jazz style

parts.note: stride is a jazz piano style with a leaping left hand
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Written works about a kind of jazz that produces a grating sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and grating, a sound that is shrill and harsh.

clue.text: Some have a trophy to put away

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the answer is a run within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A few people have a cup that they must store.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is an idiom for eating it, especially in quantity.

clue.text: Youth given directions to catch old horse

indicators.note: the two directions enclose the other pieces as if catching them

parts.note: N and E are the compass directions north and east
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: A young person is told which way to go to capture an aged horse.
explanation.walkthrough: O and NAG go between N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonage is the period of legal minority, before coming of age, i.e. youth.

clue.text: Distracted, following Frenchman with nervous twitch

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
Rene is a typical French man's name
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Someone frantic after meeting a Frenchman who has an involuntary spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frantic and wildly agitated, close to distracted in the older sense of driven out of one's wits.
